clue.text: P.C. having papers with rhymes to stick on it

parts.note: two words that rhyme with the 'stick' that follows: a pick and a candle's wick
a club is a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A policeman with documents is told to fasten some verses onto something.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria lets 'stick' work twice: PICK and WICK are its rhymes, and then the stick itself is a CLUB, set on after them ('on it').
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional society in Dickens whose posthumous papers give the novel its title is abbreviated P.C. here.

clue.text: A railway in an old capital, the 27 with buttons

indicators.note: the railway words are placed inside the old capital's name

parts.note: Peking is the old Western name of Beijing, China's capital

explanation.surface: A train line running through a former capital, with the best of something wearing buttons.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 across is VERY BEST, so the definition reads 'the very best with buttons': a king of his kind. A Pearly King is a London costermonger leader whose suit is covered in pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pearly King is a traditional London street-trader figure, a 'king' or top man, in a suit sewn with mother-of-pearl buttons.

clue.text: Smoking remains of clothing in which its cut is disguised

indicators.note: the clothing word sits within the disguised letters that follow
a disguise changes how letters look, so these are rearranged

parts.note: garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Someone's outfit has been altered so that a cut in it is hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' looks like it describes the clothing but signals the shuffle; 'in which' says the garment word sits inside the shuffled letters, not around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The stubs left after cigars are smoked are the remains of that smoking.

clue.text: Uneconomic activity reported in the centre

indicators.note: said aloud, so a word for the centre is heard as another word

parts.note: the waist is the body's middle

explanation.surface: Inefficient work is said to be happening in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste is activity that squanders resources, the opposite of economic use.

clue.text: Pointers to heaven from rich cruise ship with two missing?

indicators.note: the answer is made from a reshuffle of the cruise-ship words, less what goes missing

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something pointing skyward comes from a luxury liner that has lost a couple of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange RICH CRUISE SHIP with two I's (II, Roman two) 'missing'; the clue's question mark admits there is no clean anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Church steeples rise heavenward and seem to point the way to heaven.

clue.text: Film addition to young conservatives' house

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an addition to a letter
YC stands for Young Conservatives, the British party's youth wing

explanation.surface: A movie adds something to the youth Tories' building.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is the famous Hitchcock film, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Beast with former rider reported fraternising with groom

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, a beast

indicators.note: said aloud, so the rider's word is heard as a sound-alike

parts.note: a knight was a mounted soldier of the past

explanation.surface: An animal and an old horseman are said to be mixing with a stable lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a stable hand beside the beast and rider, but it is the bridegroom; a stag night is his party with his male friends before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag night is the evening a bridegroom spends carousing with his friends before marrying.

clue.text: See 1 across
Single French city to be inverted

indicators.note: the two halves of the city name swap places, turning it upside down

parts.note: Lyon is a city in France

explanation.surface: A lone French city is to be turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' here swaps LY and ON rather than reading the name backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Only as an adjective means sole or single, as in an only child.

clue.text: M.P.C., with a universal outburst against America, has fellows backing drug

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
a gust is a sudden outburst
US is America

indicators.note: going backwards, so the fellows' word is read in reverse

parts.note: dons are university fellows
grass is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An MP who blew up against the US has colleagues supporting a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: M.P.C. is Member of the Pickwick Club; 'against' just sets US beside GUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus Snodgrass is one of the club members in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, the would-be poet.

clue.text: 1 and his man are identical, accepting turn to the left

indicators.note: taking in, so the turn goes inside the word for identical

parts.note: things that are identical are the same
U as in a U-turn
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Two people are said to be alike, provided one swings left.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is Pickwick: Mr Pickwick and his manservant Sam Weller share the first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Mr Pickwick and his servant Sam Weller bear this first name in the Dickens novel.

clue.text: Reminiscent about Soviet farm?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a collective was a state farm in the USSR

explanation.surface: Nostalgia concerning a farm in the old USSR.
explanation.definitionFit: Recollective means given to recollection, remembering the past, which is being reminiscent.

clue.text: Housekeeper's escape seen in colour in the cinema

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god, a keeper of the house

indicators.note: placed within, so the escape letters sit inside the colour

parts.note: green is a colour
ESC is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A housekeeper's getaway is spotted in a coloured film at the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Housekeeper's' is just 'is'; LAR, a Roman god of the home, is the housekeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The big screen is a common idiom for the cinema as opposed to television.

clue.text: Exaggerated picture of rhotacist's alley cat heard during treatment

indicators.note: inside, so the spoken cat goes within the treatment

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the cat is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: someone with this speech quirk turns L into an R sound, so 'alley cat' comes out as 'arry cat'

explanation.surface: A cartoon of a stray cat, as pronounced by someone with a speech defect, is heard in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhotacism is a speech quirk over the letter R; here it turns L to R.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is a picture that exaggerates its subject's features for comic effect.

clue.text: Skirting awful mess, agree with valuation

indicators.note: going round the edges, so the agree word surrounds the jumbled mess

parts.note: to assent is to agree

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone avoiding a terrible mess goes along with a price estimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirting' reads like avoiding the mess, but it means going round its edges: the agree word wraps the jumble that 'awful' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation or estimate of value, a valuation.

clue.text: Maker of weapons giving kings increased power

parts.note: K and R (rex) are both abbreviations for king
up means increased, as prices are up

explanation.surface: An arms manufacturer gives monarchs greater strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Krupp was the German armaments firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Krupp was the great German steel and armaments dynasty, a maker of weapons.

clue.text: Co-operates with performances at dance

parts.note: plays are stage performances
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone goes along with shows at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom meaning to co-operate or go along with others.

clue.text: See 9
M.P.C. with seafood following a line other than accepted

indicators.note: placed after, so the seafood comes after the rearranged letters
made other than it is, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a winkle is an edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A member eats shellfish while taking an unorthodox line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges A LINE THAN; 'accepted' rounds out the surface ('other than accepted').
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Winkle is the sporting member of the club in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Food for journey to the East

parts.note: a trip is a journey
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Provisions for a trip to the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, the stomach lining of cattle, is a food.

clue.text: Fish in bands keep smells in drains

indicators.note: the fish goes inside the bands

parts.note: straps are bands
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Fish caught in straps keep the odours in the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the things do rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench trap is a U-bend in a drain whose water seal keeps foul smells down.

clue.text: Put away in point-to-point

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
W, west, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Stash something during a horse race over jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; here it is read as one compass point, TO, then another.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to put it away or pack it.

clue.text: Stretch that Eve did?

definitions.meaning: ... is the old past tense of spin, from 'When Adam delved and Eve ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A span is a stretch of time or distance, and also the archaic past tense of spin, which Eve did.

clue.text: See 21
In which road is a bus expected to make a delivery?

clue.text: See 18
Light for footballer to do all he can

parts.note: a Very light is a signal flare
George Best was a famous Northern Irish footballer

explanation.surface: A floodlight for a football player so he can give his utmost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do all he can' = 'do his very best'; 'Light' is the Very light flare.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's very best means doing all one can, the utmost effort.
